blocks.title: Your computers, reachable from each other
blocks.description: One panel for both directions: this machine as something you can log in to from a phone or another computer, and your other computers as places you can drive from here.

showcase.assistant_reply: Session handed to ToDesk — accept it in its window.

items.title: Code and password, one row
items.description: Type the far side's 9-digit code and its temporary password, press connect. ToDesk opens the session in its own window.

items.title: This machine's code, in the clear
items.description: The code you read out loud is shown plainly, copyable, and re-readable after the client restarts. Only passwords are masked.

items.title: Stays reachable
items.description: Start-with-Windows is a switch here, and the panel says what unattended access still needs from ToDesk itself.

items.title: Hang up properly
items.description: Disconnect runs ToDesk's own -exit, so the session does not linger; the panel then reports the client as gone instead of "connected".

items.title: Per-capability consent
items.description: Five agent tools, each with its own switch in diagnostics — plus the host's command grant underneath.

items.title: Says where the picture is
items.description: The remote desktop renders in ToDesk's window. The panel starts the session and never pretends to mirror it.

items.title: Install ToDesk and sign in here
items.description: The plugin drives the copy you already use; it does not ship or install ToDesk.

items.title: Grant ToDesk.exe once
items.description: The host asks per command: allow it in Settings → Plugins → ToDesk → commands, or in the install approval.

items.title: Connect with code + password
items.description: Read both off the far machine. The password is the temporary one ToDesk shows there.

blocks.content: The picture and the mouse live in ToDesk's own window. This plugin can start and end a session, not draw it.
